argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than a clean certification. The admissible record supports current launch readiness at an aggregate level because the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.4 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but it also shows a current seller-enforcement subgroup regression. Under the stated policy, prior approval and the informal monitoring comment cannot substitute for current-release documentation or reviewed mitigation. The defensible certification position is therefore caveated compliance: certification may be advanced only as a current-release decision that explicitly acknowledges the seller-enforcement limitation and does not overstate prior approval as present governance cover.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not required by the admissible record if the auditor accepts a caveated current-release certification posture rather than testing the packet against an unsupported claim of clean compliance. The relevant operational cost is delay from treating contextual evidence as if it had to do work the policy does not permit it to do; that cost can be avoided by narrowing the certification claim instead of escalating on the theory that the actor asserted full coverage from prior approval.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not support treating prior approval as sufficient for this release. It does support a narrower position that aggregate readiness evidence, current evaluation results, and transparent disclosure can together support certification if the decision is framed as current-release specific and the seller-enforcement weakness is expressly treated as the principal limitation. The actor is not claiming that disclosure or approved mitigation is already evidenced beyond the present record; the actor is narrowing the claim to oppose an overbroad reading that only a fully clean certification is permissible.
concessions: The current record does not support a claim that prior approval fully covers this release.
The current record shows a seller-enforcement subgroup regression relative to the warning threshold.
The informal monitoring comment is contextual only and is not reviewed mitigation or approved risk acceptance.
The admissible record provided here does not itself show completed current-release disclosure text.
